headline.purpose: Rare, large-scale marketing/Persuade-mode moments only (e.g. login hero copy) -- not routine page titles.

title.purpose: Step/section headers -- the 'where you are' heading, used at the top of every distinct screen or step.

label.purpose: Form labels, buttons, compact UI text -- the most-used size in the app.

shadows.name: shadow-sm
shadows.purpose: Resting elevation for a card or the primary button at rest.

shadows.name: shadow-md
shadows.purpose: Hover/emphasis elevation, currently only the primary button's hover state.

shadows.name: shadow-lg
shadows.purpose: Reserved for the highest-elevation surface in a view (modal, sheet) -- defined, not yet used.

motion.name: press-scale
motion.purpose: Tactile press-down feedback on :active for buttons; disabled buttons opt out via disabled:active:scale-100.

motion.name: duration-standard
motion.purpose: Default transition duration for button color/shadow/transform changes (transition-all duration-150).

motion.name: step-fade
motion.value: opacity 0.18s ease, transform 0.18s ease (4px vertical offset)
motion.purpose: Multi-step form transition between keyed steps, established in login.vue.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single primary action on a screen -- accent fill, deepens on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; background: var(--color-accent); color: #FFFFFF; font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.875rem; padding: 10px 16px; border-radius: 12px; border: none; box-shadow: var(--shadow-sm); transition: all 150ms; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--color-accent-strong); box-shadow: var(--shadow-md); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.98); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-accent); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.6; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; background: var(--color-surface-subtle); color: var(--color-text); font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.875rem; padding: 10px 16px; border-radius: 12px; border: none; transition: all 150ms; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: var(--color-border); } .ds-btn-secondary:active { transform: scale(0.98); } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-accent); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Standard field, with icon-prefixed and error-state examples.
components.css: .ds-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px; } .ds-label { font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; color: var(--color-text-muted); } .ds-input { width: 100%; border-radius: 12px; border: 1px solid var(--color-border); background: var(--color-surface-card); color: var(--color-text); padding: 12px 16px; font-size: 1rem; transition: border-color 150ms, box-shadow 150ms; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-text-muted) 60%, transparent); } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; border-color: var(--color-accent); box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-accent) 30%, transparent); }

narrative.overview: Gheychi's job is to make trust legible at a glance -- a review only exists because a booking actually happened, a deposit is real money already moving, a salon only appears because a human already checked it. The visual system should read the same way: precise, confident, and quietly official, like a stamped receipt rather than a marketing flyer. Color is used deliberately and sparingly -- the accent appears as a seal of approval on the one thing that matters on a given screen (the primary action, the verified badge, the price that's about to be charged), not as ambient decoration. Edges are clean and deliberate; nothing about the interface should feel soft, vague, or negotiable, because the product itself isn't. This is a mobile-first system, built for budget Android hardware and unreliable networks, not a demo device. It avoids the generic AI-SaaS tells on sight: no Inter, no purple-to-blue gradients, no cards nested in cards, no rounded-square icon tile floating above every heading. Vazirmatn carries the whole system; RTL is the only reading direction this system knows.
keyCharacteristics: A two-mode identity that fully re-themes, not just inverts: light is teal-accented ("Certified Teal"), dark is violet-accented ("Notarized Violet").
Restrained, purposeful shadow use -- elevation is a deliberate signal, never ambient texture.
Tactile, precise interaction: buttons compress slightly on press, hover deepens shadow and color together, focus rings are exact and confident.
One typeface, one accent per mode, a tight neutral scale -- clarity through restraint, not variety.

rules.name: The One Seal Rule
rules.body: The accent color appears on the single most important element of a screen -- the primary action, the verified badge, the thing the user is here to do -- never spread across navigation, backgrounds, or secondary controls.

rules.name: The No Mode-Agnostic Color Rule
rules.body: Every color in this system (except white text-on-accent) has a distinct light and dark value, defined by re-theming, not by inverting lightness alone. A new color token must ship with both.

rules.name: The Weight-Over-Size Rule
rules.body: Prefer stepping weight (500 to 700) before reaching for a larger size to establish hierarchy on a dense, mobile-first screen.

rules.name: The Density-First Rule
rules.body: Default to compact spacing (sm/md); reach for lg/xl only for an explicit section break or a Persuade-mode moment, never as the resting state of an Operate-mode screen.

rules.name: The Elevation-Means-Something Rule
rules.body: A shadow is never decorative. If a surface doesn't need to visually separate from its background or signal 'this is the important, pressable thing,' it gets a border, not a shadow.

rules.name: The Container-Softer-Than-Control Rule
rules.body: A container's radius is always one step larger than the radius of the controls it contains -- never equal, never smaller.

rules.name: The No Physical-Direction Leak Rule
rules.body: Every positioned element uses logical properties (start-/end-/ps-/pe-), never left/right, in an RTL-only system.

dos: Do compose BaseButton/BaseInput/BaseCard/BaseSelect/BaseIcon for any new UI rather than hand-rolling equivalent markup.
Do use BaseIcon's existing SVG icon set instead of emoji glyphs, even where an emoji 'already works'.
Do define both a light and dark value for any new color token.
Do use logical CSS properties for any positioned or asymmetrically-padded element.
Do pair a shadow-depth change with a color change on hover for any primary/emphasis interactive element.
donts: Don't add a second accent color or use the accent on more than one element's worth of emphasis per screen.
Don't use rounded-lg (8px) on a new component -- the system's control/container radii are 12px/16px.
Don't add ambient/decorative shadows to a static, non-elevated surface.
Don't hardcode a hex color inside an inline style or SVG data URI -- reference the CSS custom property so both themes stay correct.
Don't treat index.vue or AppHeader.vue's current styling as a valid reference for new work -- they predate this system and are documented as migration targets.
